

There's a subtle bug: In the diamond topology, a cell may get visited twice via different dependency paths, potentially being appended to `order` twice (the intermediate recomputation uses stale values, and unnecessary callbacks might get triggered). Fix `propagate` so that each cell is added only once:

<tool_call>
<function=edit>
<parameter=new>
func (c *cell) propagate() {
	const (
		unvisited = iota
		inProgress
		done
	)
	state := map[*cell]int{c: inProgress}
	var order []*cell
	var visit func(*cell)
	visit = func(x *cell) {
		switch state[x] {
		case unvisited:
			state[x] = inProgress
			for _, o := range x.outs {
				visit(o)
			}
			state[x] = done
			order = append(order, x)
		case done:
			// already scheduled to recompute in this pass
		}
	}
	visit(c)
</parameter>
<parameter=old>
func (c *cell) propagate() {
	pending := map[*cell]bool{c: true}
	var order []*cell
	var visit func(*cell)
	visit = func(x *cell) {
		if !pending[x] {
			return
		}
		delete(pending, x)
		for _, o := range x.outs {
			pending[o] = true
		}
		order = append(order, x)
	}
	visit(c)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
